official.deadline_note: The university states the deadline as 'October 20 of the academic year for which the scholarship is to be awarded'. The published 2026/2027 schedule opens applications on 1 October, so the operative window for the current round is 1-20 October 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year; applications submitted 1-20 October in USOSweb
official.status_note: The university's published 2026/2027 Scholarship Fund schedule lists the Rector's Scholarship round for 1 to 20 October with electronic submission only.
benefits: Monthly cash stipend for the duration of the academic year, paid from October to June
Paid twice a month, on the 15th and the last day of the month
Tax-exempt in Poland and not declared in the annual tax return
Can be combined with the scholarship from the Rector's Fund for Olympiad Participants
eligibility: Enrolled in first-cycle, second-cycle or long-cycle Master's studies at the Jagiellonian University (including foreign students)

First year of first-cycle or long-cycle Master's studies and admitted in the year of taking the matura, who is a laureate of an international Olympiad or a laureate/finalist of a central-level Olympiad, or a medalist in at least a Polish Championship-level sport competition
Higher years: outstanding academic performance, scientific or artistic achievements, or sports achievements at least at national level

First-year second-cycle students may apply on the basis of the GPA and achievements from the final year of their first-cycle studies, provided they began the Master's in the year they completed the Bachelor's
Foreign students admitted from the academic year 2019/2020 onward, regardless of citizenship or study terms

Not available to a student holding a Master's degree (even if obtained abroad) or a Bachelor's degree when re-enrolling in first-cycle studies, nor to conditionally enrolled students, students who repeated a year without completing the next one, or students who resumed studies after removal from the student list
requirements: Applications must be submitted online only via the USOSweb system using the 'Sign and submit' function; no paper submission to the Scholarships Office is needed
All achievements must be confirmed with an appropriate certificate attached electronically to the application in USOSweb
Achievements reported after submission of the application are not taken into account
The weighted GPA must be verified by the student's programme office in the USOS system
The scholarship holder must provide a bank account denominated in Polish zloty (PLN) with a bank operating in the territory of Poland
documents: Certificates confirming every circumstance cited in the application, attached electronically to the application in USOSweb

For first-year second-cycle students who completed first-cycle studies at another university: a certificate confirming the arithmetic GPA for the last year of first-cycle studies, excluding the bachelor's thesis defence grade
Documents drawn up in a foreign language must be submitted with a translation into Polish (a regular translation suffices for the Rector's scholarship)
selection_criteria: Points-based system awarding points for the grade average plus academic, artistic and sports achievements
Awarded to a maximum of 10% of students in a given programme/specialisation; one common ranking list covers full-time and part-time students together
In the first year, every student who meets the Olympiad or Polish Championship medal criteria and applies is granted the scholarship - the number of scholarships is not limited
Only achievements and the grade average obtained in the previous academic year are evaluated

Ties are resolved in order by points for achievements, then ECTS credits obtained, then the grade average over the entire course of studies, then the admission result for first-year second-cycle students
coverage: Monthly cash stipend for nine months, October to June
Scholarships are tax-exempt and are not declared in the annual tax return in Poland
Transferred to a bank account in PLN maintained in a bank operating in the territory of the Republic of Poland
application_method: Go to the 'For everyone' tab, then 'Applications'
Choose the Rector's Scholarship application and use the 'sign and submit electronically' function
Attach certificates for every achievement cited, then submit before the 20 October deadline
official.application_route: Apply online in USOSweb (For everyone > Applications) using 'Sign and submit electronically'; nothing is filed with the Scholarships Office.
official.study_mode: full-time and part-time (one common ranking list for all forms of study)
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign students admitted from the academic year 2019/2020 onward may apply regardless of citizenship; students who began earlier must study under the rules applicable to Polish citizens
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the university states the Rector's scholarship may be received by any student admitted from 2019/2020 onward regardless of citizenship or study terms
official.duration: Awarded for the academic year, in principle 9 months (October to June); in some academic years the Rector may extend payment until July
official.description: The Rector's scholarship is a form of financial support granted to students (including foreigners) in first-cycle, second-cycle and long-cycle Master's studies for outstanding academic performance, scientific, artistic or sports achievements, paid monthly from the university Scholarship Fund.
official.program_type: Merit-based university scholarship from the Jagiellonian University Scholarship Fund (stypendium rektora)

living_cost_coverage - no statement of what the stipend is intended to cover

verification.notes: Read the Rector's Scholarship page, the scholarships-for-international-students page, the Rector's Scholarship FAQ and the 2026/2027 Scholarship Fund application schedule on stypendia.uj.edu.pl; eligibility, deadline, ranking rules and payment mechanics confirmed, no monetary figure published.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an in-study merit stipend, not an entry scholarship: you must already be enrolled at UJ and be able to document achievements from the academic year just finished, because points from earlier years, language certificates and school olympiad awards are explicitly excluded. The window is ten days (1-20 October) and the cap is 10% of students in your programme, so a good GPA alone rarely wins - the points that decide it are publications, active conference participation, artistic output or national-level sport medals. Ask your programme office to have your weighted GPA calculated in USOS before you submit, because the committee ranks the figure staff enter, not the one you type.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled UJ students from their second year onward with a high weighted GPA plus documented publications, conference papers, artistic works or national-level sport results.
application_readiness_checklist: Log in to USOSweb in the first days of October and locate the Rector's Scholarship form under 'For everyone' > 'Applications'
Ask your programme office to verify your weighted GPA in USOS and resolve any discrepancy with the programme coordinator before the decision is issued
List every achievement from the immediately preceding academic year and attach the matching certificate electronically; add missing documents after submission if they arrive late

Check your achievements against the published list of items that earn no points (student-organisation activity, Erasmus stays, summer schools, certificates, unpublished papers, conference organisation, Rector's/Dean's awards)
Open a PLN account at a bank operating in Poland before October so the first payment is not delayed
common_rejection_risks: Counting achievements from before the start of studies or from years other than the immediately preceding one
Assuming a language certificate, conference organisation role or Erasmus stay earns points - the university lists all of these as scoring nothing
Repeated or conditionally enrolled years, which disqualify the application outright
Missing the 20 October cut-off: late applications are paid only from the month of submission and never retroactively
Being ranked outside the 10% quota for the programme/specialisation in higher years
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is a cash award only - tuition, accommodation in Krakow, health insurance and travel stay on you, and UJ publishes no figure, so budget for full living costs without assuming any number.
document_audit: Every achievement needs its own certificate attached to the application in USOSweb; an undocumented achievement is simply not accepted and does not sink the rest of the file
Foreign-language documents need a translation into Polish - a regular translation is enough here, unlike the social scholarship's sworn translation
First-year Master's students from another university need an arithmetic-GPA certificate for the last bachelor's year with the thesis defence grade stripped out
Multi-page documents must be uploaded as a single file containing all pages
alerts: Applications are ranked by points, not by submission order, but the deadline is absolute at 20 October
You may hold the Rector's Scholarship for only one programme if you are enrolled in two, and you must tell the office which one
Combining it with a KPO scholarship is forbidden and a KPO declaration forces repayment of the Rector's scholarship in full
A student on leave may keep the scholarship, but cannot receive it for the year of study that followed the leave
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Enrol and get USOSweb access, then file one signed electronic application per academic year between 1 and 20 October with all certificates attached; the programme office confirms the GPA, the committee scores, and payment starts the month after the decision is collected.
